t.3.28.1: To Khara, who stood chariotless with mace in hand, the greatly splendid Rāma spoke words that were harsh, though gentle at the outset.
t.3.28.3: One who is a terror to living beings, cruel and a doer of wicked deeds, does not endure, even if he be lord of all three worlds.
t.3.28.2: By one standing in the midst of a great army thronged with elephants, horses and chariots, a most dreadful deed has been done, a deed abhorred by all the world.
t.3.28.4: O night-roamer, all people kill the one who commits a cruel deed hateful to the world, just as they kill a wicked snake that has come near.
t.3.28.5: Whoever commits evil deeds out of greed or desire and does not come to his senses falls and sees his own end, just as the brāhmaṇī lizard meets its end from a hailstone.
t.3.28.6: O Rākṣasa, what fruit will you gain by slaying the illustrious ascetics who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest and walk the path of dharma?
t.3.28.7: Those who do evil deeds, the cruel ones despised by the world, do not long endure after attaining sovereign power, like trees whose roots have rotted away.
t.3.28.8: The doer of a sinful deed surely reaps its terrible fruit when the time has come round, just as a tree bears its seasonal flower.
t.3.28.9: O night-roamer, in this world the fruit of sinful deeds is reaped before long, just as with poisoned foods once they have been eaten.
t.3.28.10: O night-roamer, I, the king, have come to take the lives of those who commit terrible evil and desire what is hateful to the world.
t.3.28.11: For today the gold-adorned arrows released by me will tear through you and sink in, as serpents enter an anthill.
t.3.28.12: Those who walked in dharma and were devoured by you in the Daṇḍaka forest, them you shall follow today, slain in battle together with your army.
t.3.28.13: Today let the supreme sages whom you harmed in the past, now standing in their celestial chariots, behold you slain by my arrows and dwelling in hell.
t.3.28.15: Thus addressed by Rāma, the enraged one, his eyes red with fury, then replied to Rāma, laughing, overwhelmed by wrath.
t.3.28.14: Strike as you please and make every effort, O basest of your race; today I shall bring down your head like a palm fruit.
t.3.28.16: Having slain mere common rākṣasas in battle, O son of Daśaratha, how can you praise yourself with your own lips, you who deserve no praise?
t.3.28.17: Those bulls among men who are valiant or mighty, proud of their own splendor, say nothing boastful to you.
t.3.28.18: But it is the base and undisciplined, the disgraces of the kṣatriyas in this world, who boast to no purpose, just as you, Rāma, are boasting now.
t.3.28.19: What hero in battle, proclaiming his lineage, would himself utter his own praise at so unfitting a moment, when the hour of death has indeed arrived?
t.3.28.20: In every way your shallowness has been laid bare by your boasting, as by a blazing fire of kuśa grass that only looks like gold.
t.3.28.21: But you do not see me standing here, bearing my mace, unshakable like an earth-sustaining mountain, a peak laden with minerals.
t.3.28.22: Mace in hand, I am fully able to take your life in battle, just as Antaka, noose in hand, takes the lives of even the three worlds.
t.3.28.23: Granted, much could be said to you, but I will not say it, for the sun may set, and then there would be a hindrance to the battle.
t.3.28.25: Having spoken thus, Khara, utterly enraged and wearing splendid armlets, hurled that mace at Rāma, blazing like a thunderbolt.
t.3.28.26: Hurled from Khara's arm, that huge blazing mace reduced trees and shrubs to ashes and went toward him.
t.3.28.24: Fourteen thousand rākṣasas have been slain by you; today, through your destruction, I shall wipe away their tears.
t.3.28.27: As that blazing mace, like the noose of Death, came hurtling toward him through the sky, Rāma cut it into many pieces with his arrows.
t.3.28.28: That mace, shattered and split apart by the arrows, fell to the surface of the earth, like a she-serpent brought down by the power of cudgels, spells and herbs.
